design: Hybrid = PAC-NeRF official dynamic stage (50+100 Adam iterations, official lr) started from the SAME static NeRF + initial-velocity checkpoints as the default run (<scene>_v11), with E, nu (and tauY) initialised from our model's calibrated prediction (bgsub, triplet t0, 3-seed ensemble, leave-one-scene-out offset; docs/v3g/pn_results/OURS.json) instead of the config defaults (torus E=1e5 nu=0.1; bird E=1e3 nu=0.1; playdoh E=1e5 nu=0.4 tauY=1e3; cat E=1e3 nu=0.2 tauY=1e2). Control = the default run's own dynamic stage (camera sampling RNG differs; a same-RNG default restart control torus_v11_rs was abandoned after 3 OOMs on the shared GPU).
metrics: Loss is a single random camera per iteration and too noisy for a reach-the-same-loss criterion (both runs 'reach' the default's final smoothed loss at the first full-length iteration, 51). We therefore report reach-and-stay criteria on the parameter trajectory: first iteration after which log10 E stays within 0.05/0.1 of GT and of the default run's own final E (GT-free), and the same for tauY. Wall-clock per iteration differs between runs because of GPU sharing, so iteration counts are the comparable quantity.
end_to_end_note: Under the official protocol the dynamic stage always runs a fixed 150 iterations and the static NeRF (6000 iterations) and velocity stages do not depend on the physical-parameter init, so end-to-end wall-clock is unchanged by a better init; savings would only materialise with early stopping.
